children: Homebuilding stocks have faced sustained selling pressure this year, and Pantheon Economics said there is “no relief in sight” for homebuilders’ stock prices as higher mortgage rates, weakening affordability and elevated inventories weigh on the sector.

Against this backdrop, a screen of homebuilding stocks based on their Relative Strength Index identifies 11 names with the lowest readings, suggesting they have experienced comparatively strong selling pressure. Installed Building Products
tops the list with an RSI of 34, followed by Dream Finders Homes

The broader weakness in homebuilders has been significant. Pantheon Economics noted that the Dow Jones US Select Home Construction Total Return Index underperformed the S&P 500 Total Return Index by 23 percentage points in both 2024 and 2025.
That relative weakness has continued this year, with the homebuilders index down 5% on a total-return basis compared with a 14% gain for the S&P 500.

posting RSI readings of 37 and 38, respectively. LGI Homes

Pantheon Economics said recent new-home sales data offers limited evidence of improvement. July sales were revised up to 643,000 from 607,000 previously, while August sales were preliminarily estimated at 684,000, an eight-month high.

However, the firm cautioned that the August estimate has a 90% confidence interval of ±20 percentage points around the reported 6.4% increase, meaning the underlying trend could be closer to flat and remains subdued.

Meanwhile, the NAHB survey’s expected single-family home sales index fell to 37 in September from 43 in August, its lowest level since January 2023, suggesting builders are anticipating weaker demand ahead. PulteGroup
round out the screen, with RSI readings of 42, 43 and 43, respectively.
The housing backdrop could create additional pressure on builders’ margins. Pantheon Economics expects new-home sales to weaken as renewed increases in mortgage rates weigh on affordability.

Homebuilders have already been cutting prices to support sales, with the median price of a new single-family home down 2.6% year-over-year in the three months through August. At the current pace of sales, it would take about 8.5 months to clear existing unsold inventory, compared with a 60-year average of six months.

The RSI is a momentum oscillator that ranges from 0 to 100, with readings below 30 generally considered oversold and readings above 70 viewed as overbought. While none of the stocks in the screen has fallen below 30, their relatively low readings point to notable recent selling pressure as the sector faces the prospect of weaker sales and further margin compression.
